evidence.reason: Verified staged Journal_Entry saves with the logical-field protocol: a stage opens idempotently by client token; ordinary sections travel as bounded parts; a section too large for any part sends its complete manifest in a part and then each bounded 128000-byte fragment under it. Manifests, offsets, digests, totals and sealed contents are validated before commit, and immutable field-version references plus old-version Revision references are installed atomically with the whole save. Part, fragment and manifest replays are idempotent and conflicting replays are refused. A committed stage keeps a compact receipt, so a lost commit response is reconciled by reading the stage and replaying the commit returns the original item without saving twice; the client retries lost part and fragment responses with the same bytes. Tests cover a 600000-character ASCII section, a 600000-emoji section, two million code points, label spans crossing fragment boundaries, heavily escaped text, mixed inline and logical sections, missing and mismatched fragments, refused batches leaving no current pointer, stale and unchanged edits, and no staging, section, revision, manifest or fragment row above 512000 bytes. Existing journal round trips and identities remain exact. No deployment or production certification is claimed; end-to-end property ownership remains 57.6.

evidence.reason: Verified that the upload screen keeps what a Member entered across a reload without fabricating a File. With a form scope, each file’s title, caption, Origin, name, size, SHA-256 once computed, upload ID, attempt number and the group ID are mirrored into this tab’s storage before transfer begins and on every edit (never the bytes). After a reload a completed upload is revalidated against GET /uploads/{id} without the local file; one the sweeper removed fails alone with a reason, and a transfer cut off by the reload is checked with the server (finished uploads are settled as complete) or fails alone. A file whose bytes are gone is re-chosen through an input that checks name and size, and the SHA-256 when known, before the upload restarts; every other field survives. Each start attempt and each completion is a keyed write, so a lost completion response is reconciled from the Worker’s record and the upload itself, and a lost start response removes the orphan and asks for a retry. Retry and removal act on one file and leave the others’ uploads and metadata intact. A blocked submit, including Enter in a field, moves focus to the file-specific reasons. Item, Reply and Attachment forms use the scoped hook and forget their uploads when sent or discard them when discarded. Browser tests cover reload after completion and after failure, reselection (wrong name, wrong contents, correct file), a reload during a transfer, independent retry/removal, a lost completion response and the keyboard-blocked submit. The incremental Web Worker hashing, whole-number XHR progress and 60-second stall behavior are unchanged and keep their tests. Rights choices are not part of this screen: a new file starts with Rights Status Unknown and rights are set on the Attachment screen (30.8), so none are stored here. Explicit server drafts remain with task 64. No deployment or production certification is claimed.

tasks.title: Build the inline previews in `apps/app/web/src/files/preview/`

evidence.reason: Verified that every preview reads only what it needs through a Member-bound Download_Link and names why it cannot show a file. A shared transport fetches the link through the ordinary authorized route, renews it before its 15-minute life ends or once when storage refuses a read, never sends credentials to storage, and caps every body: text logs ask for the first decimal megabyte by Range and are cut at that size even when a server ignores the Range, and a response is cancelled as soon as its limit is reached. CSV is streamed through Papa Parse: a scanner that follows quotes splits complete records, the header and 1,000 data rows are shown with the next record as a one-row lookahead, and the transfer is cancelled when the answer is known. The preview distinguishes more rows exist, end of file, and a budget-limited unknown remainder, with the 32 MiB scan, 256 KiB record and 2 MiB buffering limits from the Resource_Profile, and it never shows a quoted cell cut short. PDFs are read by PDF.js through a range transport of our own, so every range uses the refreshing link and counts against the 16 MiB cache budget; the document is canvas-only with no annotation layer, scripting, XFA or auto-fetch, keeps page n of N with previous, next and go-to controls, and draws pages smaller when the canvas would pass the 32 MiB decoded-image budget. Raster images are decoded only after the magic bytes match PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP and the header size fits the decoded-image budget; SVG, HTML and polyglots never become anything but an image/png blob; fit, zoom to 400% and keyboard and pointer panning remain. Damaged, password-protected, mismatched, unavailable and resource-limited files each get their own message while metadata and the full download stay available. Browser tests cover bounded transfer and early cancellation, abort, link refresh on a refused range, very long and malformed CSV records, quoted line breaks across chunk boundaries, malicious and polyglot files, a password-protected PDF, and the cache budget; Property 46 now exercises the streaming parser across random chunkings. Rendering in the SPA is controlled rendering in the Workspace, not origin isolation by itself. No deployment or production certification is claimed.

evidence.reason: Verified that Property 46 covers truthful bounded CSV scanning as well as text prefixes. Over random rows (quoted cells with commas, quotes, line breaks and non-ASCII text), random chunk sizes and random row, scan, record and buffer limits, every row shown is a complete row of the file in order and never more than the row limit; scanned bytes never pass the scan budget; end means every row was shown with nothing exceeded, more means the row limit was reached with a real lookahead row, and unknown names a budget that was actually exceeded (scan, record or buffer) and is never reported when nothing was; the transfer is always released and reading stops within one chunk of the record that decided the answer.
